EdgeLoop.description:

happens when the branch is taken once more: ``fail`` ends the run as failed
(``run.loop_exhausted``), ``continue`` ignores the loop, so the node's other open branches decide.

OrchestratorConfig.description:
An AI model that delegates the task to teams of its pool until it can answer (AO M4).

It only selects: it creates no agents and no tools, and has no tools of its own. Each chosen team
runs as a linked child run with its own budget, limits and tool approvals; the orchestrator's
decisions, reasons and the teams' results are recorded (``NodeRun.orchestration``).

OrchestratorSelect.description:
Pool selection by capability (AO M5): saved workflows whose capabilities match join the pool.

The selection is made when a run (or a published release) pins its workflows, so it is fixed and
visible in the run's snapshot: every selected member names the tags it matched. Teams are ordered
by the number of matching tags, then by name; no score is invented. Workflows with errors and the
workflow itself are left out. Teams with approval steps are offered: the orchestrator waits while
one of them waits for a person (AO M6b).
OrchestratorSelect.title: OrchestratorSelect

ToolBinding.description:
When an agent asks before calling one of its tools.

- ``auto`` (every new binding): ask when the tool does more than read.
- ``always``: ask for every call.
- ``never``: do not ask. Counts only for ``read`` tools, for ``write`` tools with a ``reason`` and for legacy
  exemptions; never for ``destructive`` tools. Otherwise it is treated as ``auto``.

A **legacy exemption** (``legacy``) is a binding that existed before S-2; it holds only for the tool version it
was bound to (``bound_version``): a new version of the tool ends it.
ToolBinding.title: ToolBinding

get.description: One template with guide, agents and the workflow a copy would get (a preview, never a run).

post.description:
Create an ordinary, independent workflow from a template; the template itself never changes.

Parts the template runs as sub-workflows or orchestrator teams are copied first, as workflows of their own;
every reference is pinned to their first version. Knowledge files are stored in the knowledge base (collection
"Examples: <name>" in the copy's language; identical files of an earlier copy are reused). Agents get model
tiers mapped to the workspace's provider. Integrations named in ``integrations`` are connected to the chosen MCP
server (only approved read-only tools); the others run in their labelled offline mode. With ``tests`` the
template's test cases become a test series of the copy; their sample files are stored as input files.

Everything is checked before anything is stored, and a copy that fails half-way leaves nothing behind.

post.description:
Check the Amazon Bedrock settings with free AWS calls only (STS ``GetCallerIdentity`` and one read of the
Bedrock control plane; no model is invoked) and store the result in the provider's ``verification``.

The connection diagnosis (``POST /api/diagnostics/connection?provider=bedrock``) runs the same check, so it also
stores the verification as a side effect and shares its rate limit.

A failed check answers 200 with ``verification.state == "failed"`` and a stable code; nothing about the AWS
identity (account, ARN, keys) is ever returned. At most one check every few seconds per workspace (429).
